comparator.name: Information Science (Informatiekunde)
comparator.sourceNotes: The dated UvA study guide sets 60 required credits in year one, 48 required and 12 restricted-choice credits in year two, and 30 open, 24 required and 6 restricted-choice credits in year three. The illustrated choices retain Regulatory Compliant Information Systems and Semantic Web in year two and Logic and Society in year three. Reflection on Digital Culture and the final project are required.

components.name: Regulatory Compliant Information Systems
components.note: Year two requires two of three courses: this course, Semantic Web and Recommender Systems. This example includes the first two named here.

components.name: Semantic Web
components.note: Builds on programming, databases and introductory logic. Basic web development knowledge is recommended.

components.name: Research Methods for Interactive Systems
components.note: Builds on descriptive statistics and applies research methods to human-computer interaction.

components.name: Systeemproject
components.note: UvA recommends advanced programming and prior Research Methods for Interactive Systems.

components.name: Keuzeruimte/minor
components.note: Choose 30 EC in the first semester of year three.

components.name: Reflectie op de digitale cultuur
components.note: Required in year three alongside the final project and one of two restricted electives.

components.name: Logic and Society
components.note: This example selects Logic and Society. Social Robotics is the other option.

components.name: Afstudeerproject BSc Informatiekunde
components.note: Complete all 60 EC from each of the first two years before starting. The Board of Examiners can grant an individual exemption.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad programme addresses computing, users and organisational information. The data option deepens mathematics and algorithms. The human-centred option develops cognition, qualitative inquiry and the study of users. Each pair clears the distinctness floor, and the three-option limit applies.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both use structured programming, collections, functions and introductory classes.
Both explore unfamiliar datasets and communicate patterns with graphics. UCR combines visualisation with data preparation in R.
Both design and query relational databases. UvA also compares other database paradigms.
Both teach formal logic, sets, relations and reasoning with proofs.
Both compare and evaluate machine-learning methods on datasets and address issues such as overfitting.
Both build and evaluate deep-learning models in Python across data types. UvA combines this with a broader data science pipeline.
Both use vectors and matrices for applied problems. UvA’s introductory course also includes calculus and probability.

comparator.note: Year two requires two of three courses: this course, Semantic Web and Recommender Systems. This example includes the first two named here.
Builds on descriptive statistics and applies research methods to human-computer interaction.

Complete all 60 EC from each of the first two years before starting. The Board of Examiners can grant an individual exemption.

notes.text: UCR combines computing, data analysis, user research and the study of organisations across several disciplines. UvA also teaches Semantic Web, information-system compliance and a sequence of dedicated system projects. Its individual final project is compulsory.

audience.programmeDescription: Information Science at the University of Amsterdam studies how people and organisations design and use digital systems. Students learn programming, data analysis and interaction design and apply these skills in team projects and an individual final project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options emphasise information and organisations, mathematical data analysis, or how people use technology. UvA combines these themes in one programme with a dedicated sequence of information-system design and research projects.
